prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core approach
- Principles: Freedom, Fairness, Trust, delivered through decentralised, accountable government and a strong “green thread” across all policies.
- Paying for priorities: Switch ~£5bn/year from low-priority spend (abolish the DTI’s subsidy model, scrap ID cards, redirect the Child Trust Fund). Introduce a 50% income tax only on earnings over £100,000 to fund three pledges: abolish tuition and top‑up fees, free personal care for the elderly/disabled, and lower local taxes by replacing Council Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people (as in Scotland).
- Faster diagnosis via whatever route is quickest; more scans/tests in community settings; publish diagnostic waits; extend exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- Free eye and dental check-ups; recruit more frontline staff; scrap central targets and cut red tape; reform NHS dentistry.
- Prevention: smoking ban in enclosed public places; nutrition standards for school meals; clearer food/alcohol labelling.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top‑up fees; restore grants for poorer students.
- Redirect Child Trust Fund to cut class sizes (infants to avg 20, juniors to 25); extend wraparound care and complete Children’s Centres.
- Ensure core subjects taught by qualified teachers; reduce high-stakes testing; stronger discipline support; better SEN provision; integrate academic/vocational routes; close FE/schools funding gap.

Crime, justice and liberties
- Scrap ID cards; fund 10,000 extra police plus 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy.
- Expand tough community sentences and Community Justice Panels; target drug traffickers; skills and work focus in prisons.
- Protect liberties: oppose erosion of jury trial and control orders; repeal flawed terrorism provisions; allow intercept evidence in court. Create a UK Border Force. Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units.

Economy and business
- Fiscal stability with independent audit of budgets; simpler, fairer taxes.
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450); raise stamp duty threshold to £150k.
- Pro‑EU, prepare to join the euro when conditions met; managed economic migration.
- Cut red tape (impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections); small business rate relief; abolish DTI; new duty to trade fairly; boost tourism with an English Tourism Board.

Pensions, benefits and families
- Citizen’s Pension: from 75, lift basic pension and re‑link to earnings, removing means tests for about a million; Local Income Tax benefits 8 in 10 pensioners.
- Maternity Income Guarantee: six months at the minimum wage rate.
- Replace CSA with Inland Revenue‑run assessment/enforcement; tailored welfare‑to‑work; better disability support (including Winter Fuel Payment parity); fair compensation for lost company pensions; reduce fraud/error via simplification.

Local communities and housing
- Devolve powers, slash inspections/quangos, protect Post Office network.
- 100,000 affordable homes on public land; favour brownfield via VAT reform; local controls on second homes.

Transport
- Streamline rail franchises; restore key upgrades; safer stations.
- Reward low‑emission cars via VED reform; support congestion charging; long‑term shift to national road pricing; free off‑peak buses for pensioners/disabled; curb major new roads; greener aviation taxes.

Rural, animal welfare, GM
- Fair dealing in food supply chains; CAP and CFP reform; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Act and Commission; no commercial GM without proven safety; support GM‑free zones; promote organic.

Europe, defence, development, Iraq
- Support EU constitution (via referendum); more democratic, effective EU.
- Armed forces: cut waste (e.g., Eurofighter tranche), improve welfare; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms export scrutiny.
- International development: reach 0.5% GNI aid by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; fairer trade, end dumping; sustainability focus.
- Iraq: war was wrong; back democratic transition and Iraqi capacity; aim to withdraw UK troops by end of UN mandate.

Green pledge
- Meet and exceed Kyoto; lead on “contraction and convergence”; 20% renewable electricity by 2020; no new nuclear replacements; zero-waste goal; strong environmental governance.
